status.summary: Retired. The inaugural UFC featherweight champion (seven straight defences; UFC Hall of Fame, class of 2023) announced his retirement in the cage after a 29-28 x3 loss to Aiemann Zahabi at UFC 315 (May 10, 2025) and made it official by laying his gloves in the octagon at UFC Fight Night in Rio de Janeiro on Oct 11, 2025. He is not in the UFC rankings. His only competition since was a 10-minute submission-only grappling match with Marlon Vera at Hype FC in Quito, Ecuador (Oct 4, 2026), which ended in a draw. Final pro MMA record 32-10 (UFC 14-9 per ufcstats); pro boxing 1-0-1. No MMA booking found as of Nov 6, 2026 (ESPN's profile still says 'Active', which looks stale).

signature: punches to the body (KO of Jeremy Stephens with body punches, 2018; 21 of 25 body strikes vs Merab Dvalishvili, 26 of 33 vs Jonathan Martinez)
knee in the clinch (KO of Chad Mendes, UFC 142, 2012)
stuffing takedowns: 98 of 107 UFC takedown attempts against him failed
weaknesses: output fades in championship rounds: rounds 4 and 5 of 5-round fights run at 0.72 and 0.56 of his round-1 output
four UFC KO/TKO losses (Conor McGregor 2015, Max Holloway twice in 2017, Petr Yan 2020)
out-thrown: opponents attempt 10.1 sig strikes per minute vs his 7.9 career; Zahabi out-landed him 99-68
can be pinned on the fence without being taken down: Bautista logged 7:15 and Dvalishvili 5:06 of control with 0 takedowns between them
age 40; lost his last two bouts
style.summary: In his UFC years Aldo is a patient, accurate counter-puncher with elite takedown defence and a punishing body attack. He lets opponents lead and makes them pay, but in recent years he has been out-worked over 15 minutes and fades in long fights. His famous low-kick game from earlier eras is barely visible in the UFC data (6% of attempts to the legs).

moves.notes: Weights are relative within each target group, as src/director.js uses them: head moves sum to 1, body to 1, legs to 1. spinning, knee and elbow are separate rates for occasional specials. fighters.json time-decayed attempt split is 77.1% head, 17.3% body and 5.6% leg (landed 63.7/25.4/10.9; career 79.8/13.9/6.2). Body share is above the bantamweight average of 14.1%, and leg share is well below the 9.7% average. No web scouting source could be read in the first pass, so the within-group splits are judged from the dataset alone; the Nov 6 web pass found only Wikipedia's general description (Muay Thai striking and leg kicks, with defensive wrestling), which fits the takedown-defence data but did not change the splits. Hooks lead the body group because his body work is a defining feature in the data: the Stephens KO was 'Punches to Body At Distance', and body strikes are 20.7% of his career landed. The head group is a generic boxer split. The leg group is split evenly because the data says nothing about calf vs inside kicks. knee 0.04 reflects the Mendes clinch-knee KO. Low confidence.

engine_notes.note: Takedown defence is 91.6% career (9 of 107 allowed) and 96% time-decayed: the best TDD of anyone in this batch. Merab Dvalishvili went 0 for 16 and Bautista 0 for 10.
5-round pace by round, relative to round 1: 1.00, 1.13, 1.07, 0.72, 0.56 (weights 60/55/54/42/38 minutes). A clear championship-round fade.
He still has knockdown power: knockdowns on Rob Font (2 in 2021) and Aiemann Zahabi (round 3, 2025). His career rate is 0.28 per 15 min.
Decayed striking is negative: 4.07 landed vs 4.94 absorbed per minute. His opponents' accuracy against him is 45.5% decayed vs 41.6% career, so his defence has slipped with age.
